items.grounds: Re-derived from the shipped row and the staged bytes. The row's boundary_rationale ends on the single sentence naming its back seam ('This span winds down at oshb:Isa.51.11, under its own parashah SAMEKH mark, witnessed in a single source'), names nothing that opens at web:Isa.51.12, and its boundary_evidence_refs carry neither web:Isa.51.12 nor oshb:Isa.51.12; strongest_rejected_alternative weighs only the interior Isa.51.10|Isa.51.11 question. The mark claim itself re-derives: the single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.8 and oshb:Isa.51.11, and under owner law the Prophets parashah layer is tier-3 weak corroboration, never a driver, so the row's only stated back-seam warrant is a class that cannot warrant a seam. The seam is nonetheless byte-correct: oshb:Isa.51.12 opens on אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.51.12, byte tier), a doubled first-person divine self-identification answering the community's appeal to Yahweh's arm, עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte tier), and the next shipped row already carries that onset as its own tier-1 front-seam driver. The row's digits re-sweep clean: the doubled onset עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י (oshb:Isa.51.9, byte tier) is byte-unique to oshb:Isa.51.9 (sweep: 1 verse at byte tier) and matches עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י (oshb:Isa.52.1, byte tier) from accent_stripped tier down (sweep: 2 verses); the imperative's skeleton עורי (skeleton tier) stands as a whole token 3 times in oshb:Isa.51.9 (sweep: 3 tokens in that verse); הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י (oshb:Isa.51.17, byte tier) is unique at every tier (sweep: 1 verse); שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ (oshb:Isa.51.11, byte tier) stands at byte tier in exactly 3 verses (oshb:Isa.35.10, oshb:Isa.51.3, oshb:Isa.51.11; accent_stripped tier adds oshb:Isa.22.13 for 4). Verdict: a defective warrant on a load-bearing edge whose cut is right - medium confirmed; not high because no boundary is wrong and no load-bearing claim is byte-false, not low because the sole named warrant is an inadmissible driver rather than a missing disclosure. The proposed field repair is the right remedy; no span change.

The byte facts re-derive exactly as filed: oshb:Isa.51.12 addresses a plural in מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.51.12, byte tier) and then a feminine singular in מִֽי אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.12, byte tier); from the next verse on the marking is masculine singular - עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ (oshb:Isa.51.13, byte tier), אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Isa.51.15, byte tier), בְּפִ֔יךָ and כִּסִּיתִ֑יךָ (oshb:Isa.51.16, byte tier) - while oshb:Isa.51.14 carries no second-person marking at all; the row's prose quotes only web:Isa.51.12, web:Isa.51.15 and web:Isa.51.16, and its strongest_rejected_alternative weighs only the merge across the front seam, so the internal turn is indeed undisclosed. Both seams and both SAMEKH claims (oshb:Isa.51.11 and oshb:Isa.51.16 in the single-witness inventory) re-derive. Severity is mis-set, however: the candidate seam Isa.51.12|Isa.51.13 does not fall between two addresses but inside one syntactic chain - oshb:Isa.51.13 opens on the wayyiqtol וַתִּשְׁכַּ֞ח (oshb:Isa.51.13, byte tier, its first token), continuing וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.12, byte tier) of the verse before, so the feminine-to-masculine switch is an inflection change mid-sentence with no frame token, no vocative and no imperative at the verse head. Under the owner granularity rule that a syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one unit, that rival cannot stand as a seam, and the row's actual warrant for holding web:Isa.51.12-Isa.51.16 (one divine speaker, no frame token) is not defective. What remains is a disclosure shortfall: the internal marking turn, the untouched verses web:Isa.51.13-Isa.51.14, and the open identity of the masculine-singular addressee told לְצִיּ֖וֹן עַמִּי אָֽתָּה (oshb:Isa.51.16, byte tier) each deserve a sentence, but the proposed confidence and frontier recalibration is not compelled by a rival the bytes themselves defeat. Downgrade: real, at low, not medium.

Re-swept with the count object named each time. The three-letter consonantal root shared by שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte tier) and לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier), swept as the skeleton שמע (skeleton tier), stands as a contiguous consonantal substring in 84 verses book-wide (sweep: 84 verses; 92 token occurrences), as a whole word-bound token in 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses) and token-initially in 51 verses (sweep: 51 verses). The four-letter skeleton שמעו (skeleton tier) of the first site sweeps to exactly 30 verses (sweep: 30 verses), and the second site's skeleton לשמעתנו (skeleton tier) contains the three-letter root but not the four-letter string, so the 30-verse object cannot contain oshb:Isa.53.1 at all. The row's device_notes bind '(sweep: 30 verses book-wide)' to 'a three-letter consonantal-root tier': the digit is real but belongs to a different count object, and no sweep in the row backs the echo as offered - the finding re-derives in full. The claim sits in device_notes, is explicitly 'not a challenge to the seam', and the row's seam drivers (הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י at oshb:Isa.52.13, byte tier; לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ at oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier) are untouched, so this is a defective digit claim that is not load-bearing: medium confirmed. Either repair named in the proposal is byte-sound.

The single-witness inventory re-derives exactly as the finding states: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.53.12, oshb:Isa.54.8, oshb:Isa.54.10 and oshb:Isa.54.17, and no petuchah or setumah at any other verse of oshb:Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 (the row's four cited sites are the only sites). The closings re-collate at byte tier: oshb:Isa.54.8 ends on אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.8, byte tier), oshb:Isa.54.10 on אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.10, byte tier), oshb:Isa.54.17 on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.17, byte tier) - three of the four cut points the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative assigns to the rival - while the fourth rival cut, after אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.54.6, byte tier), and the opening signature אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses at byte tier, re-derived) carry no mark. The interval oshb:Isa.54.8 to oshb:Isa.54.10 is two verses. So 'wide intervals rather than at the signature closings individually' is false on the row's own cited data, and 'corroborating a longer reading over a finer one' inverts what the layer shows: every mark inside the chapter falls on a rival cut point and none falls anywhere else, so the layer (tier-3 weak corroboration under owner law, never a driver either way) aligns with the finer reading, not the longer one. The seam driver is the byte-grounded vocative onset רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier), untouched by this defect; the mark claim is defective but not load-bearing - medium confirmed. Field repair as proposed; no span change (the layer's alignment with the rival is corroboration only and cannot itself move a seam).

oshb:Isa.55.5 carries 17 tokens and opens on הֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier); the prefixed title וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier) occupies token positions 14-15, preceded by יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier). So 'the prefixed form heading web:Isa.55.5' is byte-false as a position claim. The underlying tier claim re-derives: קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.54.5, byte tier) collates against oshb:Isa.55.5 at accent_stripped tier only, not at byte tier, exactly as the row says. The defect is confined to the position word in device_notes, on a continuity device the row already subordinates to the invitation-cry onset at web:Isa.55.1, so it is not load-bearing for the row's own seams - but it is not inert either: read as written it would put a verse-initial divine title at the head of the very verse whose seam status (Isa.55.4|Isa.55.5 against Isa.55.5|Isa.55.6) is contested in the neighbouring rows, so it is a byte-false factual claim rather than a mechanical slip. Medium confirmed; the proposed one-word repair cures it.

The Hebrew the sentence supports re-derives in full: oshb:Isa.55.5 runs masculine singular from תֵדַע֙ through יְדָע֖וּךָ אֵלֶ֣יךָ to אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ and פֵאֲרָֽךְ (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier); oshb:Isa.55.2 closes on נַפְשְׁכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.55.2, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.55.3 carries אָזְנְכֶם֙, נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם and לָכֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier), all plural; oshb:Isa.55.1, oshb:Isa.55.4, oshb:Isa.55.6 and oshb:Isa.55.7 carry no second-person suffix (oshb:Isa.55.1 and oshb:Isa.55.6 carry plural imperatives only), so 'exactly one of the seven verses' is true. The defect is in the clause attached to it. The staged corpus carries one English witness (the WEB) against the MT; 'neither witness's English marks' and 'both render every surrounding pronoun the same way' assert a rendering comparison across two English witnesses, one of which does not exist in the staging - an unsourceable claim, false against the staged witness set, placed inside the rear-seam warrant sentence. One correction to the finding's characterization: the clause does not use the translation as corroboration - it notes, negatively, that the English cannot show the turn, which drives nothing - so the tier-4-corroboration prong is overstated; the phantom second witness is the real defect, and it is enough on its own. Not load-bearing (the seam stands on the pointed bytes and the seven-verse sweep), so medium rather than high; a false witness claim inside the warrant sentence is more than a mechanical slip, so not low. Confirm medium; deleting the clause, as proposed, cures it.

The bytes re-derive as filed: a plural addressee through oshb:Isa.55.3 (אָזְנְכֶם֙ and נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם, oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier), no second person in oshb:Isa.55.4, a wholly masculine-singular oshb:Isa.55.5 (from תֵדַע֙ to פֵאֲרָֽךְ, oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), and a return to plural imperatives at דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier); הַטּ֤וּ (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier) is likewise verse-initial inside the preceding span. The single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.55.5 and nothing at oshb:Isa.55.4 - tier-3, never a discriminator. The row's boundary_rationale never mentions a cut before oshb:Isa.55.5, and its strongest_rejected_alternative addresses a rear rival (web:Isa.55.10-Isa.55.13 as a doxology closure) - not, as the finding's grounds say, an undivided-chapter reading, which is the preceding row's rival; the claim that the nearer rival is undisclosed stands either way. The finding overstates one point: a byte discriminator does exist - oshb:Isa.55.6 opens on the imperative דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier), whereas oshb:Isa.55.5 opens on the presentative הֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), which matches הֵ֛ן opening oshb:Isa.55.4 (oshb:Isa.55.4, byte tier) at accent_stripped tier, a paired presentative onset binding the singular verse to the Davidic-witness verse before it; so of the two turn positions only the cut before oshb:Isa.55.6 carries an imperative onset. The row names that imperative form-class but never deploys it against the nearer rival, which is live (a verse-boundary cut on the row's own addressee-number driver class, unlike a mid-sentence switch), so the front-seam warrant is defective, not merely under-disclosed: medium confirmed. The proposed field repair is right; no span change.
